title: 9 Cursor rules I steal from senior devs
caption: The .cursorrules lines that separate shipped code from AI slop. Save this.

slides.headline: 9 Cursor rules I steal from
slides.sub: Paste these into .cursorrules. Thank me later.

slides.title: Read before you write
slides.body: "Always read the full file before editing it. Never edit code you haven't read in this session." Kills the #1 cause of AI regressions.

slides.title: Explain, then change
slides.body: "Before any edit, state in one sentence what you're changing and why. If you can't, don't edit."

slides.title: Match the codebase
slides.body: "Mirror existing patterns, naming, and structure. Consistency beats your preferred style."

slides.title: Smallest possible diff
slides.body: "Change only what the task requires. No drive-by refactors, no reformatting untouched lines."

slides.title: Tests are not optional
slides.body: "For any logic change, write or update the test in the same edit. No test, no done."

slides.title: Ask before deleting
slides.body: "Never delete files, env vars, or config without explicitly asking. Deletions are irreversible in a hurry."

slides.title: No premature abstraction
slides.body: "Don't build the generic version until there are 3 real callers. YAGNI by default."

slides.title: Surface assumptions
slides.body: "List every assumption you made before I run this. Wrong assumptions caught early are free."
